thread:
alex: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a compact response shape for /v1/rerank to reduce JSON bloat when clients send 100+ candidates. Idea: send back a slim array of scores + minimal metadata instead of full candidate objects.
priya: curious — how slim are we talking? we still need provenance for audits.
mike: +1 on provenance. maybe a compact envelope with a `scores` array and a separate `meta` bag keyed by candidate_id. e.g.
```json
{
  "scores": [0.921, 0.47, 0.12],
  "candidate_ids": ["c1","c2","c3"],
  "meta_refs": ["m1","m2","m3"]
}
```
priya: that reduces repeated payload but adds indirection. console/telemetry wise we lose per-candidate fields unless client derefs meta. are we ok with that for first rollout?
ajex: @alex (typo) alex: i think first rollout should keep enough to map back to trace. include `trace_id` at root and keep `meta_refs` optional. ops-bot: rerank-service-canary deployed v2.1-slim to canary (10% traffic)
jordan: telemetry question — our quota accounting measures 'candidate-units' today. if we change shape, do we change counting? e.g., current billing = candidates * model_weight. if client now uses compact, server still does same compute but client traffic is smaller. should quota reflect compute or payload size?
mike: quotas must reflect compute. compact shape is only a wire optimization. we should not change candidate-units. but console should show a new column "payload_bytes_saved" for adoption tracking.
priya: model selection interplay: if we fall back to smaller model (eg. rerank-small) under load, do we still return same compact shape? yes, but we need to annotate which model produced the scores. propose `model_tag` string at root.
alex: proposal: response envelope shape v2-slim = { trace_id, model_tag, scores[], candidate_ids[], meta_refs? } + optional `score_precision` field. default precision = 3 decimals.
mike: precision debate — some consumers rely on exact floats for tie-breakers. is 3 decimals ok? maybe make it opt-in: clients can request `precision=full` in query or `precision=3` to save bytes. also we must log in telemetry whether precision was reduced.
priya: agreed. add `precision_mode` to the response and a per-request telemetry tag `rerank.precision_mode`. console-team: we can add a per-route rollout toggle in Console under "Rerank response format" to switch canary groups between "full" and "slim". UX: surface warnings if a route has third-party clients that don't declare support.
jordan: for routing & quotas: when using model hedging (attempt large model then fallback), how do we report candidate-units? we charge for both attempts today. do we want to keep that? some teams asked to only charge final model.
alex: that's a policy question. ops prefers conservative (charge both) to avoid under-accounting. product prefers best-effort charging. tradeoff: hedging boosts tail SLO but doubles cost. we should not change in this rollout. document as "no change to candidate-units for hedged requests".
mike: telemetry instrumentation checklist:
- tag: rerank.response_shape = slim|full
- tag: rerank.model_used = <model_tag>
- metric: payload_bytes_saved per route
- metric: score_precision_mode counter
- trace: include candidate sampling if client asked for subset
priya: console-team, can we add a small graph showing "avg payload bytes" + "avg candidate count" per route? that's the key driver.
console-team: yes we can add it to the per-route panel. would need a backend exporter that emits payload_bytes_post_compression and candidate_count. we'll wire up by next sprint.
alex: rollout plan:
1) implement v2-slim in service behind feature flag `rerank.payload.compact` (server default off)
2) expose `precision` request param and `precision_mode` telemetry
3) enable canary at 5% for internal routes only (no public customers)
4) collect payload_bytes_saved + validation errors for 48h
5) if <0.1% validation errors and no perf regressions, expand to 25% and enable console toggle for allowed external routes
priya: btw validation errors to watch: mismatch in candidate ordering when client expects stable ties, missing provenance fields, and deserialization failures for clients that expected full candidate objects.
mike: add a server-side safety fallback: if a client declares `accepts_slim=false` (via header), return full shape. default to accept slim.
jordan: can we add a compatibility header `x-rerank-format: slim-v2` so downstream gateways can opt into transformations? that's useful for partners.
alex: yes `X-Rerank-Format` will be the header. log it in APIGW too.
priya: final ask: add an audit event when `meta_refs` is used without `meta` available (should only happen if proxied incorrectly). ops-bot: alert rule created: rerank.slim.missing_meta > 1/min triggers pager to eng-platform on-call.
mike: ok, I'll wire the telemetry and docs. alex — want me to open the PR for the shape + server fallback?
alex: please. include tests that compare deterministic ordering between full and slim shapes. also add a console experiment entry for tracking.
priya: thanks — ping us when PR is up, I'll review the precision and console parts. :thumbsup:
